entities.summary: Marcus Servilius Pulex Geminus, a Roman senator and military commander, played a pivotal role in the Second Punic War and the early decades of the second century BC. He was the son of Marcus Servilius Isauricus, a consul, and was educated at the Academy of Athens. Following his father's death, Geminus succeeded him in the consulship in 173 BC and led the Roman army against the Carthaginians in the war. He was a skilled orator and strategist, known for his bravery and leadership, and was praised by his contemporaries for his military prowess. Geminus's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he was revered by his descendants for their military achievements. He was the first of the Servilius family to be granted the title of consul, and his family's reputation continued for generations. The Servilius family's association with the Roman aristocracy and their military conquests are still remembered today. Geminus's life and achievements serve as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Roman Republic and its impact on modern Western civilization. Despite the passage of time, his name remains synonymous with bravery and leadership, and his contributions to Roman history continue to be studied by scholars and historians.
